OpenStax, Psychology §5.1 — sensation versus perception, and the role of attention in what reaches awareness

visual.title: Sperling's grid and the moving bottleneck
visual.alt: Sperling's twelve-letter grid flashed for fifty milliseconds, with whole report recovering four or five letters and a tone-cued single row recovering three of four, implying about nine were available; a curve of letters still available against the delay before the cue, falling from nine to the whole-report level by one second; the three filter models placed along a processing stream, with Broadbent's filter before meaning, Treisman's attenuator, and the Deutsch-Norman late bottleneck after semantic analysis; and four failures of attention — inattentional blindness, change blindness, the psychological refractory period and the vigilance decrement.
visual.caption: Partial report is the whole experiment in one idea: cue the row before the image fades and almost all of it is still there. What limits report is decay plus attention, not how much the eye took in.
